newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish pulp derivative trade delayed again.
newsitem.headline: Finnish pulp derivative trade delayed again.

text.p: Trade in pulp derivatives on the Finnish Suomen Optioporssi Oy (SOP) options exchange will not start on schedule on Monday, a SOP executive said on Thursday.
"It is 99 percent certain that trade will not start on Monday," Vice President Jaakko Soini said by telephone.
In a statement, SOP said trading will start as soon as there are at least 30 clearing accounts.
Soini said "less than 10" members had so far signed up for FOEX (Finnish Options Exchange), and he declined to speculate when trading would finally start.
Trade in the pulp derivatives was originally intended to start on September 9.

"FOEX is ready for an immediate market start. However, there seems to have been a confusion about the terms under which securities brokers and banks can participate in trading and clearing of commodities," SOP said in the statement.
The statutes and rules of FOEX for trading the pulp contract were officially approved by the finance ministry on September 6, it said.
FOEX is providing the market with PIX Pulp benchmark price information on Reuters page SOPI.
The latest PIX benchmark price will be released every Monday at 1200/0900 GMT. The September 16 price was $563.04 per tonne, up from an average of $556.24 in August, the exchange said.
"Information for calculation of the benchmark price is supplied by more than 30 companies from 11 different countries," SOP said.

"We believe that this project will provide the pulp and paper industry with the much needed financial tool for combating the adverse effects of the volatile pulp market, affecting producers, buyers and financial institutions alike," it said.
